claims.text: [failure-modes] A partial failure leaves a state the next run can repair. An interrupted append leaves a torn tail, which is reported as incomplete and named. It blocks appends until drop_torn_entry, and that call is logged with who ran it. drop_torn_entry writes a temporary file and renames it over the log; if it crashes at the rename, the torn log is left byte-identical. Done.

notes:
Gaps that need the owner (not fixed, to keep scope):
1. R42 and R43 as written need production callers. The seven case actions (import, profile change, override, preview, pack write, sign-off, purge) must call CaseLog.append with an expected position, and sign-off must call require_intact and refuse with first_bad. Neither exists anywhere in src, and both depend on C3/C5/C6 tasks. The task decomposition should decide one of two things: (a) T12 is accepted as the primitive plus P15, with R42/R43 end-to-end traced to the sign-off and override tasks, or (b) T12 stays open until those land. Re-attempting T12 alone cannot pass the R42/R43 'no production caller' check. This is the reason for attempts 1-2 failing, and there is 1 attempt left.
2. Removing the head entry (truncating the last complete line) cannot be detected from the file alone, and the docstring says so. The sign-off and pack must record the head position and hash, and verify must compare against them. That is a design item for C6.
3. Deleting the .lock file while it is held lets a second writer lock a new inode. The case-root permissions (0700, R31) are the mitigation and belong to the case-root task.
4. Observability, operability and docs gaps: there is no structured event log line, red banner or runbook entry for the broken or torn refusal yet; these belong with the C5/C6 callers. There is no CHANGELOG file in the repo.
5. The Windows msvcrt lock path is untested here (Linux runner only).
6. Append cost is O(log size) because it re-verifies the whole log, about 42 ms at 2000 entries. That is fine for expected case sizes, but if logs grow past ~10k entries, cache the verified head per (inode, size).
